name: Explicit / Information Manipulation / Information Gathering
description: Direct requests aimed at obtaining data, credentials, or identity confirmation from the recipient.
criteria: Explicit requests for credentials, passwords, or account details
Requests for identity confirmation or verification
Direct or indirect questions aimed at harvesting personal or organisational data

name: Explicit / Information Manipulation / Information Control
description: Instructions to manage system access, permissions, or credential configurations.
criteria: Instructions to modify account preferences or security settings
Requests to update or change credentials
Directives to assign or revoke system access

name: Explicit / Resource Acquisition / Direct Financial Gain
description: Explicit requests for money transfers, bank account details, or payment credentials.
criteria: Requests for wire transfers or cryptocurrency payments
Requests for bank account or payment credential details
Demands for immediate financial action

name: Explicit / Resource Acquisition / Indirect Resource Acquisition
description: Requests for non-monetary resources with clear transferable value such as gift cards, equipment, or admin rights.
criteria: Requests to purchase gift cards and share codes
Requests to order or ship physical equipment
Requests to grant system or administrative access

name: Explicit / Trust Establishment / Identity Establishment
description: The sender explicitly asserts their name, role, title, or organisational position to establish credibility.
criteria: Explicit introduction of name and professional title
Claims of institutional affiliation or seniority
Personal identity assertion used to justify the request

name: Explicit / Trust Establishment / Legitimacy Creation
description: The email invokes a known organisation, brand, official process, or compliance requirement to appear legitimate.
criteria: Reference to a known brand or institution to justify the request
Claims of mandatory compliance, policy, or regulation
Use of official-sounding language or process framing

name: Explicit / Call to Action / Direct Action Requests
description: Explicit instruction for an immediate specific action such as clicking a link, filling a form, sending information, or confirming details.
criteria: Imperative verbs directing immediate action (click, fill, send, confirm, call)
Clear deadline attached to the action
Action is specific and immediately executable

name: Explicit / Call to Action / Indirect Action Facilitation
description: The email sets up conditions for a future required action without issuing the direct command yet.
criteria: Preparatory instructions that enable a future step
Request for a reply or acknowledgement that triggers next steps
Framing that implies a mandatory follow-up action is coming

name: Implicit / Authority
description: The email exploits hierarchical power, invokes institutional authority, or threatens consequences for non-compliance to compel action.
criteria: Reference to a superior's approval or directive
Threat of consequences for non-compliance
Invocation of institutional hierarchy to pressure action

name: Implicit / Social Proof / Herd Mentality
description: The email claims that most or everyone has already complied, implying the recipient should follow the group.
criteria: Explicit claim that colleagues or peers have already acted
Quantified statements of prior compliance to create social pressure
Framing the recipient as an outlier for not yet complying

name: Implicit / Social Proof / Diffusion of Responsibility
description: The email uses collective framing to dilute individual agency, implying this applies to everyone and reducing personal accountability.
criteria: Emphasis that the request applies to all employees or everyone
Collective framing that removes the sense of individual choice
Language that makes non-compliance feel like a group failure

name: Implicit / Social Proof / Moral Duty
description: The email appeals to the recipient's prosocial values, framing compliance as protecting or benefiting others.
criteria: Framing compliance as an act of protection for colleagues or the organisation
Appeal to shared responsibility for collective safety or wellbeing
Altruistic framing that makes refusal feel selfish

name: Implicit / Liking, Similarity & Deception / General Deception
description: The email presents a scenario or claim that is objectively false or fabricated to manipulate the recipient.
criteria: Objectively false claims presented as fact
Fabricated scenarios used to justify the request
Impersonation of a legitimate entity or process

name: Implicit / Liking, Similarity & Deception / Deceptive Relationships
description: The email falsifies a prior relationship, fakes a referral, or claims false familiarity to lower the recipient's guard.
criteria: False claim of a prior meeting or conversation
Fabricated referral from a known contact
False claim of personal or professional relationship

name: Implicit / Liking, Similarity & Deception / Liking & Similarity
description: The email exploits genuine or claimed shared characteristics, expertise, or identity to build manipulative rapport.
criteria: Claim of shared professional identity or expertise
Appeal to shared background, values, or experience
Flattery or praise used to create reciprocal goodwill

name: Implicit / Distraction / Scarcity
description: Exploits perceived limits on available time or resources to prompt action.
criteria: Explicit deadline or countdown attached to the request
Urgency language ('immediately', 'now', 'last chance')
Threat of negative consequences if action is not taken within a time window
Claims of limited spots, quantities, or availability
Framing the offer as exclusive or available only to a select group
Scarcity used to prevent deliberation

name: Implicit / Distraction / Overloading
description: The email deliberately overwhelms with multiple simultaneous demands or dense complex information to bypass rational judgment.
criteria: Multiple concurrent action requests in a single email
Dense or complex information deliberately exceeding processing capacity
Cognitive overload used to prevent critical evaluation

name: Implicit / Distraction / Strong Affect
description: The email deliberately triggers fear, alarm, or excitement to bypass rational analysis.
criteria: Fear-inducing language about account suspension, security breach, or legal action
Excitement or reward framing designed to cloud judgment
Emotional intensity used to prevent careful evaluation

name: Implicit / Distraction / Need & Greed
description: The email appeals to exceptional financial reward, exclusive status, or personal enrichment opportunity.
criteria: Promise of disproportionate financial gain
Appeal to desire for exclusive status or recognition
Framing compliance as a path to personal enrichment

name: Implicit / Commitment, Integrity & Reciprocation / Integrity
description: The sender explicitly signals their own honesty, transparency, or good faith to lower the recipient's guard.
criteria: Explicit personal claim of honesty or good faith
Proactive disclaimer of malicious intent
Transparency performance used to disarm suspicion

name: Implicit / Commitment, Integrity & Reciprocation / Consistency
description: The email invokes the recipient's past behaviour, stated values, or established role identity to create a sense of obligation to comply.
criteria: Reference to the recipient's past actions or commitments
Appeal to the recipient's stated or assumed values
Role-based expectation framed as a consistency obligation

name: Implicit / Commitment, Integrity & Reciprocation / Commitment
description: The email creates obligation through explicit coercion, prior agreements, or role-based expectations with consequences for non-compliance.
criteria: Explicit threat if the recipient does not comply
Reference to a prior agreement or obligation
Role-based duty framing with escalation consequences

name: Implicit / Commitment, Integrity & Reciprocation / Reciprocation
description: The email implies that a prior favour or service has been performed, creating a felt obligation for the recipient to return it.
criteria: Explicit or implied claim that the sender has done something for the recipient
Framing of the request as a return of a favour
Effort or sacrifice claim used to create social debt
